documents.title: Park 2 opening lifted visits 35% and merch per cap 8% — cast overtime overshot by EUR 2.9M
documents.source_ref: SDP Attendance & Labour — daily turnstiles × cast hours, Apr–Oct 2026
documents.excerpt: Disney Adventure World (Park 2) visits are 35.1% above the same months of 2025 since the new lands opened on 29 March, and merchandise per cap is up 8.2% to EUR 17.08. Cast overtime ran 10.0% of hours against a 5.5% standard on Park 2 peak days: EUR 2.9M above budget, concentrated in F&B and attractions.

documents.title: Heatwave week in July cut visits 10.8% below forecast and lifted beverage mix to 41% of F&B
documents.source_ref: SDP Daily Attendance Forecast — ML forecast with weather exogenous variables
documents.excerpt: From 14 to 20 July 2026 daily visits ran 10.8% below forecast (about 56,500 a day) as temperatures passed 36°C. F&B covers fell less than visits and beverages rose from 33% to 41% of F&B sales, so F&B per cap rose about 8% while admissions fell for the week.

documents.title: UK & Ireland visits 8.8% below budget on GBP/EUR — offset by French domestic and Annual Pass growth
documents.source_ref: SDP Guest Market Mix — booking source × country of residence × FX
documents.excerpt: UK & Ireland visits are 8.8% below budget since June as GBP/EUR moved from 0.84 to 0.88 and package prices rose for UK guests. French domestic visits are 4.9% above budget and Annual Pass visits about 9% up, recovering most of the admissions gap but with lower hotel attach.

documents.title: Resort Hotels RevPAR EUR 3.3 below forecast — occupancy, not ADR
documents.source_ref: SDP Hotel Revenue — 7 hotels, occupancy × ADR, booking-curve pace
documents.excerpt: October 2026 RevPAR was EUR 325.6 against EUR 328.9 forecast. ADR held at EUR 369 (+EUR 6 vs forecast), but occupancy was 88.2% against 90.5%: Davy Crockett Ranch (−EUR 16.6 RevPAR) and Hotel Santa Fe (−EUR 15.0) ran 6–7 points behind on weaker UK package pickup.

documents.title: UK visits −8% and energy +30% would take EUR 43.6M off FY2027 EBITDA
documents.source_ref: SDP Scenario Analysis — energy kWh × price, cast hours × pay rate
documents.excerpt: UK & Ireland visits −8% (−EUR 19.4M with 60% flow-through) and electricity repriced 30% higher from January (−EUR 24.2M) take FY2027 EBITDA from EUR 558.9M to EUR 515.3M (16.9%) before mitigation. A 3.8% NAO pay round would cost a further EUR 15.0M vs the 2.5% budget assumption.
